---
title: "Poverty and deprivation"
description: "How many people are at risk of poverty or cannot afford basics, and the effect of social welfare."
---

The CSO measures poverty in three main ways. People are at risk of poverty if their household income, adjusted for the size of the household, is below 60% of the national median. They experience deprivation if their household cannot afford two or more of eleven basic items, such as a warm waterproof coat or keeping the home adequately warm. They are in consistent poverty if both are true.

In 2025, 12.6% of people were at risk of poverty, 15.1% experienced deprivation and 4.7% were in consistent poverty. None of the three has changed much overall since 2020, although deprivation rose to 17.3% in 2023 before falling back.

{{< chart poverty-rates >}}

## The effect of social welfare

Social welfare payments lift many people above the poverty line. In 2025, 33.2% of people would have been at risk of poverty based on their income before social welfare payments. After them, the figure was 12.6%.

{{< chart poverty-social-transfers >}}

## Compared with the EU

Eurostat compares countries using a combined measure, the share of people at risk of poverty or social exclusion. It counts people in low-income households, in households that cannot afford a number of basic items, and in households where adults work very little.
